lines: 2 packages are imported by their root in src, so the whole barrel is reachable and the bundler keeps whatever it cannot prove unused:

@nextcloud/vue: 1,522,926 B in 201 modules, 17.8 % of the static path of maps-main.js, imported by its root in 25 files: components/AppNavigationContactsItem.vue (NcActionButton, NcAppNavigationItem, NcCounterBubble), components/AppNavigationDeviceItem.vue (NcActionButton, NcAppNavigationItem), and 23 more.
axios: 46,020 B in 52 modules, 0.5 % of the static path of maps-main.js, imported by its root in network.js (default) and views/App.vue (all, spread).
Importing the module that is used instead of the package root lets the bundler drop the rest of the barrel.
ncmake's lint-vue-imports workflow gates exactly this specifier for @nextcloud/vue, so this finding is that red check with a byte figure attached.

32 components of @nextcloud/vue are delivered although no file in src names them, no other dependency names them and no component named by either imports them: 70,302 B, 1.9 % of the static path of maps-publicFavoriteShare.js, next to 16 components the source names, 2 that other dependencies name and 11 those pull in.
NcRichText 10,845 B, NcDateTimePicker 8,586 B, NcRelatedResourcesPanel 6,822 B, NcActionInput 6,812 B, NcBreadcrumbs 5,616 B, NcColorPicker 4,393 B, and 26 more.
These arrive through the root import: under a barrel the whole component set is reachable, so the bundler must keep it. Per-component imports leave it free to drop what the app never names.

16 delivered files look like a webpack or CommonJS bundle. Their internal structure is not derivable from the artefact, so each counts as one file and the chunk figures below say nothing about what is inside them.
Every delivered file in js carries a source map, so every byte can be charged to the package and the module it came from.
